finding.summary: queued() can return 1-tuples from blank or malformed lines in queue.txt (e.g. empty lines or lines without a space separator), because tuple(line.split(" ", 1)) on a line with no space yields a single-element tuple. Callers that unpack as key, folder = queue.pop(0) (in cli.py start_queued() and the display rendering) will raise ValueError: not enough values to unpack, breaking queue processing and screen rendering.
finding.fix: Filter out lines that do not contain a space before splitting, e.g. return [tuple(line.split(" ", 1)) for line in p.read_text().splitlines() if " " in line] if p.exists() else []

label: false_positive
label_reason: only `status.save_queue` writes `queue.txt`, always as `KEY FOLDER` lines via a temp file and rename, so blank or space-less lines cannot occur.
notes: finding.line moved 41 -> 45: at raised_sha 812f904 the `tuple(line.split(" ", 1))` the finding describes is at status.py:45 (41 is the `def queued` line); the review cited the wrong line.
